title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Improving the Work Mechanism of Presiding Judges' Meetings in People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Guiding Opinions on Improving and Perfecting the Working Mechanism of the Principal Judge Conference of People's Courts (For Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2018] No. 21

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Guiding Opinions on Improving and Perfecting the Working Mechanism of the Principal Judge Conference of People's Courts (For Trial Implementation) are hereby issued for your earnest implementation in light of actual circumstances. Any problems encountered during implementation shall be promptly reported to the Supreme People's Court.

November 28, 2018

Guiding Opinions on Improving and Perfecting the Working Mechanism of the Principal Judge Conference of People's Courts (For Trial Implementation)

To fully implement the judicial accountability system, accurately apply the law, unify adjudication standards, and improve trial quality and efficiency, the following opinions are put forward in light of trial practice regarding the improvement and perfection of the working mechanism of the principal judge conference of people's courts.

1. A people's court shall improve and perfect the working mechanism of the principal judge conference to provide guidance and reference for judges in accurately applying the law in the trial of cases, promote the unification of adjudication rules and standards, summarize trial experience, and improve trial management.

2. The working mechanism of the principal judge conference may be established within internal trial business departments such as civil, criminal, administrative, state compensation, and enforcement, and may also be established across trial business departments or trial teams.

3. The principal judge conference shall be composed of full-time judges of the court. Judges participating in the meeting shall have equal status, rights, and responsibilities.

Depending on the议题 of the meeting, experts, scholars, deputies to the People's Congress, members of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, and other relevant professionals may be invited to participate in the meeting and express opinions.

4. For cases falling under any of the following circumstances, the collegial panel or the sole judge may request discussion by the principal judge conference:

(1) Cases that are of a new type, difficult, complex, or have significant social impact;
(2) Cases where adjudication rules or standards need to be unified or have universal guiding significance in the application of law;
(3) Cases where the proposed adjudication result is inconsistent with the adjudication rules or standards of similar effective cases from the same court or a higher court;
(4) Cases where there are significant differences of opinion among members of the collegial panel;
(5) Cases where the presiding judge holding the minority opinion deems it necessary to request discussion;
(6) Cases where a reversal, remand for retrial, or a request for retrial or designation of retrial is proposed;
(7) Other cases that need to be submitted for discussion.

In accordance with relevant provisions on trial supervision and management, the president, vice presidents, and division heads may decide to submit the four types of cases stipulated in Article 24 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Improving the Judicial Accountability System of People's Courts to the principal judge conference for discussion.

5. The collegial panel or sole judge hearing a case shall prepare necessary materials and deliver them to the participants before the principal judge conference is convened.

6. Judges participating in the meeting may express their opinions in order from low to high based on judicial rank and seniority, or, depending on the circumstances of the case, judges familiar with the specialized knowledge involved in the case may express their opinions first; however, the chairperson shall express his or her opinion last.

7. At the conclusion of the meeting, the chairperson shall summarize the discussions, form discussion opinions, and record them in the meeting minutes. The meeting minutes shall be fully documented in the case file and on the case handling platform in accordance with regulations.

8. The collegial panel or sole judge hearing a case shall independently decide whether to adopt the opinions formed during the discussion of the principal judge conference and shall be responsible for the final outcome of the case.

9. The president, vice presidents, and division heads may, in accordance with their trial supervision and management authority, require the collegial panel or sole judge to reconsider the case based on the opinions formed during the principal judge conference. If, upon reconsideration, the majority opinions formed by the principal judge conference are not adopted, the president, vice presidents, and division heads shall submit the case to the adjudication committee for discussion and decision in accordance with regulations.

10. Persons attending the principal judge conference shall strictly observe trial discipline and shall not disclose the meeting topics, case information, or discussion contents.

11. A judge's participation in the principal judge conference may be counted toward his or her workload and included as a bonus item in performance appraisal for the judge's performance file.

12. People's courts at all levels shall strengthen the centralized management of the working mechanism of the principal judge conference, timely organize, print, and distribute meeting minutes of significant importance for forming adjudication rules, unifying legal application standards, exchanging trial experience, and guiding judicial practice. After the judgment in a case becomes effective, resources shall be shared through the publication of judgment documents, typical cases, and other means.

13. Trial business departments of the Supreme People's Court, circuit courts, and local people's courts at all levels may adopt these opinions as a reference and formulate detailed working rules based on their functional positioning, trial work needs, number of judges, number of cases, and other actual circumstances.
